chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
A Muslim is one whom people are at safety from his hand and tongue, and a believer is the one whom people trust upon their property and themselves.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a Muslim and a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith in *Mani al-Akhbar* to delineate the progressive spiritual ranks of *Islam* (submission) and *Iman* (faith) through social ethics. It establishes that while a Muslim ensures general peace through restraint of the tongue and hand, a true *Mu'min* achieves a higher station by becoming a reliable custodian of others' material and existential well-being, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal trust (*amanah*).

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
A Muslim is one whom people are at safety from his hand and tongue, and a believer is the one whom people trust (as a guardian) upon their property and (upon) themselves.
